config.consolidation: N=100 x2 seeds = 200 paired samples, lean (headline). Also N=50x2 pilot: results/horizon_rm_n50/gen_20260707_164658
config.tau_grid_note: tau 0.575 (~3.0x) added to populate the 2.8-3.2x band (a gap in the N=50 pilot)
config.qualitative_run: results/horizon_rm_qual/gen_20260708_055203 (N=6 x1 seed, --save-all-images, tau 0.4/0.5/0.65; full+SeaCache+plain+RM per-method PNGs for the sample-comparison grids)
config.method: r_pred = r_anchor + beta*lambda(t)*P(r_anchor - r_prev); v = head(front(x_t,sigma_t) + r_pred); no extra block-stack forward
config.compute_accounting: RM is free tensor arithmetic; achieved speedup == plain HorizonCache. Oracle runs add a full forward per cached step (diagnostic only, not charged).

metrics.halfdb_gains_concentration: >+0.5 dB gains are in the 2.0-2.8x band; at 3.0-3.4x RM-plain is smaller (+0.19 to +0.43) but still CI-positive
metrics.vs_seacache_safe_band: roughly doubles E56 margin (2.50x: plain +1.99 -> RM +2.90 dB; 2.74x: +2.18 -> +2.74)
metrics.overshoot_flip_3p4x: plain adaptive_* -0.17/-0.19 dB (loss vs SeaCache, CI excl 0) -> RM +0.25/+0.26 dB (win, CI [+0.11,+0.42]); at 3.03x both beat SeaCache (plain +0.43, RM +0.62)
metrics.oracle_note: secant does NOT better-predict the instantaneous true residual (frozen 0.269 vs motion 0.285, -5.6%); gain is accumulated-drift correction, not per-step accuracy
